key_findings.metal_needs_something_to_reflect: METAL_METALLIC measures 0.114 scene-linear against a 0.35 lower bound, with zero clipping. It is too DARK, not too bright: a metal reflects its environment rather than scattering, and the characterization rig has a near-black backdrop by design. The fix is a declared reflection environment, not a lower window — metals are characterised against what they reflect.
key_findings.matte_satin_reads_on_swatch_not_on_produ: matte vs satin passes characterization robustly (3 axes, controls, perturbations) but fails product observability: across five defensible P1B views, at most 1.1% of pixels differ against a predeclared 4%/10-level bar. key_findings.metric_edge_cases_caught_by_controls: the grid metric normalised before applying its occupancy filter, so minimum-value cells dropped and a perfectly correlated pattern scored 0.0. key_findings.observability_closed_by_computation_not_: the matte/satin product FAIL fell to three stacked defects, each caught by looking at evidence rather than trusting a number: (1) the boosted rim2 was a separation rim at the contract position, nowhere near the mirror direction — position, not brightness, was the root cause; (2) the first computed placement targeted the open-state tray deck and scored 0.000 because the swung-back lid stood in the camera's optical path — an occluded view is indistinguishable from a material tie, so a ray-clearance commissioning check now refuses to measure such views, with the deck pinned as its negative control; (3) the corrected closed-lid view saturated the satin frame at the transplanted energy and frac 1.000 was evidence of clipping, not sheen — one scene-linear float render calibrated the energy DOWN analytically (E = E0*0.85/peak). Final: 70.7% differing at the unchanged 4%/10-level bar, both frames unclipped, satin showing the reflected source image, matte quiet grey. Neither the bar, the geometry, nor the material definitions moved.
